finalText:
All checks pass — build clean, 23 tests green. Here's what I implemented.

**Route** — [src/routes/orders.ts](/work/src/routes/orders.ts): added `POST /orders/:id/apply-coupon`, which only parses the id and forwards `couponCode` to the service.

**Service** — [src/services/orderService.ts](/work/src/services/orderService.ts): `applyCoupon` normalizes the code (`trim().toUpperCase()`), then validates in the exact order the spec's error table requires (invalid body → order missing → not pending → coupon already applied → coupon missing → inactive → not-yet-valid → expired → usage exhausted → minimum not met). Time comes from the injected `Clock`. It computes FIXED/PERCENT discounts with floor + optional cap, then delegates the write.

**Repository** — [src/repositories/orderRepository.ts](/work/src/repositories/orderRepository.ts): `applyCoupon` wraps the three writes (order update, `coupon_redemptions` insert, `used_count + 1`) in a single `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`, rolling back on any failure. All SQL stays in the repository layer.

Wiring in [src/app.ts](/work/src/app.ts) now passes the coupon repository into `OrderService`.

**Tests** — [tests/applyCoupon.test.ts](/work/tests/applyCoupon.test.ts) covers AC-01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 08, 09, 10 plus every error code and the "no DB change on rejection" guarantees. Existing tests and schema were left untouched.

One design note worth flagging: the three-statement transaction touches the `coupons` table from `OrderRepository` rather than splitting it across two repositories, since a single atomic unit was cleaner than coordinating a cross-repository transaction.
